articleTitle: On the nature and general regularities of optical activity in planar-chiral double-layer metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The most interesting examples of various double-layer metamaterials that provide “optical activity” are presented to reveal the motivation of use of different cell topologies. The phenomena of the giant “optical activity”, existence or lack of perfect matching, multi-band phenomena, the role of higher space harmonics, and influence of space spectrum rarefying are considered and explained based on the spectral theory of opened structures.

articleTitle: Atomic functions theory: 45 years behind
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In 2016 marks 45 years since the publication of the first papers on the theory of infinitely differentiable finite solutions of a functional differential equations so-called atomic functions (AF). The review presents a brief analysis of the publications, since the first ones until now. Both individual and scientific schools investigations are considered related to the theoretical foundations and practical aspects of atomic functions usage in physics and engineering.

articleTitle: Ground-based millimeter-wave ozone monitoring in Moscow during sudden stratospheric warmings
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Results of monitoring of vertical ozone distribution at millimeter waves over Moscow during a number of mid-winter sudden stratospheric warmings that occurred over last two decades are presented. Ozone concentration in middle stratosphere over Moscow in winter months may be considered as a predictor of approaching mid-winter major stratospheric warmings.

articleTitle: Stepped Frequency Continuous Wave Ground Penetrating Radar applications
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) operating on the basis of Stepped Frequency Continuous Wave (SFCW) is analyzed for various applications with extraction of additional information about physical properties of soil and buried objects. The phase structure is obtained from the signal phase-frequency spectrum by applying the Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) to signals on the output of SFCW georadar quadrature phase detector. It has been shown that the phase gradient of a phase-frequency spectrum of signals reflected from underground layers and buried objects are determined by their electrical properties. Also it is represented some application of such GPR to detect and recognize some explosive hazards with applying algorithm of synthetic antenna aperture technique.

articleTitle: NMR & MW techniques for detection of explosive and illicit materials
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The detection of explosives and illicit substances is a very important problem nowadays. Especially, improvised explosive devices (IEDs) manufactured from homemade explosive materials has become an issue of growing importance. In this work, recent developments in the field of time domain (TD) NMR and microwave/sub-THz detection of liquid substances are reviewed. It has been shown that both TD NMR and MW dielectric spectroscopy are potentially very effective techniques to detect content of concealed liquids.

articleTitle: The qualitative theory of electron beam formation in a surface wave magnetron
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The paper presents some results of analytical design and computer modeling of electron beam formation in the surface wave magnetron. It is shown that a process of phase focusing of the re-entrant electron beam in the interaction space of the surface wave magnetron has two features associated with a concentration of RF wave energy neighbourhood of the surface of the periodical structure (vanes of anode block) and higher electron hub of space charge as compared with the classical magnetrons. On base of trajectory analysis of the electrons moving in the interaction space of the magnetron and interacting with the surface wave of periodical structure a scenario of phase focusing is considerated. The computer modeling results of the space charge distributions are shown.

articleTitle: High power THz technologies opened by high frequency gyrations covering Sub-THz to THz region
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: High frequency gyrotrons developed in FIR UF covering sub-THz to THz range have achieved operation functions such as high stabilization of frequency and power, high speed frequency modulation and frequency tunability. Such gyrotrons with functions of frequency and power control have opened new horizon of high power THz technologies, for example, high frequency DNP-NMR spectroscopy, direct measurement of hyperfine structure of positronium, activation of Boron-neutron capture therapy (BNCT), etc. The status of development and applications of high frequency gyrations in FIR UF are introduced.

articleTitle: Inverse problems of electromagnetic sounding: Gradient medium and periodic boundary
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The problems of the periodic interface profile reconstruction and the recognition of dielectric constant of the layered medium according to the values of the reflection coefficients for a finite set of probing frequencies are rather urgent in connection with the development of modern non-destructive testing methods. To solve them the original problems are reduced to the search for the optimal control (the profile of the dielectric constant) of the Cauchy problem for the Riccati equation. Construction of optimal control in the class of polynomial functions is based on the minimization of the corresponding functional. The criterion of selection of polynomial approximations for profile permittivity uses the separation of input data into Training and Testing sequences of probing frequency. An analysis of errors of the reconstruction of the imaginary part of permittivity of the layered medium was carried out.

articleTitle: High-frequency methods for applied problems of electromagmnetic wave scattering
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Numerical methods for computing scattering characteristics of complex-shaped aerial and ground objects are described. Some problems of monopulse direction finding, including radome and lens antenna influence, are solved. The numerical simulation of directional pattern of a reflector antenna with precipitations on the reflector surface was conducted in approximation of physical optics. The results of calculations are considered and analyzed.

articleTitle: Laser Scanning Microscopy of superconducting electromagnetic metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Sub-wavelength superconducting rf meta-materials have evident advantages over their normal metal counterparts for strong diamagnetism, low-loss and intrinsically nonlinear tunability with temperature, dc magnetic, and rf electromagnetic field. These microwave properties are uniquely controlled through the spatial distribution of super-fluid density in the superconductor. The technique of low-temperature Laser Scanning Microscopy (LSM) is applied to investigate local contribution of these effects onto global rf response of superconducting meta-materials having different geometry of artificially structured magnetic meta-atoms. The main capabilities of the LSM technique for noncontact spatially resolved characterization of such structures are reviewed.

articleTitle: Spatial-harmonic magnetrons with cold secondary-emission cathode: Advances and challenges
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Spatial-harmonic magnetrons with cold secondary-emission cathode are efficient high-power millimeter-wavelength oscillators. Recent advances in the development of such low-voltage magnetrons, 210 GHz tubes, and magnetrons with an extended lifetime are reviewed. Potentials for further improving the performance of spatial-harmonic magnetrons are considered as well.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave noise radar tomography
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: SAR tomography based upon MIMO concept with channels time-division is described and some results of its experimental validation using Ka-band ground based noise waveform SAR are presented. Two different linear synthetic apertures have been used for both transmit and receive antennas oriented in vertical and horizontal directions, respectively. Range resolution in SAR tomography is determined by power spectrum width of the transmitted signal, while its cross-range resolution is defined by 2D aperture dimensions and working wavelength. The approach suggested is applicable for generation of 2D and 3D coherent SAR images and radio-films provided data acquisition and signal processing in real time.

articleTitle: Resonant interaction of electromagnetic waves in the defective photon crystal bordering on conducting medium
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The effect of resonant interaction of plasma and defective electromagnetic waves in the defective photon crystal bordering on conducting medium is studied.

articleTitle: Influence of neutral winds on the formation of the F2-region of the middle-latitude magnetically quiet ionosphere
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The elements of a global picture of thermosphere circulation, the changes of value and direction of thermosphere wind over Kharkiv are calculated with use of horizontal neutral winds model HWM93. The calculations of constituent part of vertical component of ionospheric plasma velocity induced by horizontal neutral winds were made. By theoretical simulation there are calculated the altitude profiles of electron density as the taking into account the motion of the ions along the magnetic fields lines induced by the neutral winds, as without it.

articleTitle: Interference method of definition of energy gap and relaxation time of superconducting state
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: A method which allows measuring simultaneously an energy gap and a relaxation time of a superconducting state is proposed.

articleTitle: Dispersion characteristics of planar dielectric waveguide - grating system
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this work, the results of theoretical and experimental study of eigen waves of periodical system formed of planar dielectric waveguide and grating are presented. The research revealed the dispersion characteristic features that helps to understand the resonant effects which occur during the radiation forming. Moreover, the results ensure an optimization of system parameters that provides the obtaining of specific characteristics of diffraction radiation antennas.

articleTitle: Multilevel structured experiment design regularization approach for computational enhancement of compressed radar/SAR imagery
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: We address a new approach for computational enhancement of low resolution radar/fractional SAR imagery that unifies the descriptive experiment design regularization (DEDR) framework with the total variation (TV) inspired sparsity preserving (Sp-Pr) regularization paradigm. The new framework incorporates the structured projectors onto the convex solution sets (POCS) into the TV-restructured DEDR framework and solves the overall compressed image computational reconstruction/enhancement problem employing the proposed aggregated DEDR-TV-POCS strategy.

articleTitle: Research of scattering characteristics of snow crystals
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The paper analyzes the scattering of few types of snow crystals at variations of the elevation angle of the radar antenna in a wide frequency ranges.

articleTitle: MM-wave range oscillator with a multi-mirror open resonator
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The millimeter wavelength range generator with four-mirror open resonator is described. The frequency and energy characteristics of the generator are investigated.

articleTitle: The bipolar nature of the movement in the star-forming region IRAS 05553+1631
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: We present <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup>CO (J=1-0) observations of the IRAS 05553+1631. It is shown that this emission has is bipolar nature. The locations of red-shifted and blue-shifted components of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup>CO emission do not coincide with the corresponding parts of the bipolar outflow in <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sup>CO line. Origin of bipolarity in <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup>CO emission is a shift of the entire profile of molecule line.

articleTitle: Measurement resonance frequency and quality-factor of resonant cavity of Tesla-type in superconducting regime
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The article concerns the technique of effective and accurate measurement high quality-factor of resonant cavities of Tesla-type that are used in the ILC in superconducting regime. Presented key outcomes that have been obtained using specially developed computerized measuring system with a set of extra UHF parts.

articleTitle: Optimal reception of signals propagating in media with absorption and dispersion
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The features of optimal reception of signals propagating in media with the absorption and dispersion are considered. It is shown that in this case bandwidth of emission-reception should be adapted to the desired range of distances, as well as to compensate the phase distortion is introduced by medium of propagation. It is proposed using of the modified correlation functions for signal analysis in such cases.

articleTitle: Dependence of processing speed on the autodyne operation mode
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Main equations for calculation of autodyne response time constant, the boundary cutoff frequency of autodyne signal and sensitivity of a microwave oscillator are obtained. Investigations of dependence of these parameters on the oscillations mode choice and the form of an impedance characteristic of the active element are performed on the example of the Gunn diode autodyne of-8mm-range.

articleTitle: Spatial structure of five star forming regions: 121.28+0.65, 34.403+0.233, 77.462+1.759, 99.982+4.17 and 37.427+1.518
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In paper presents the results of multi-spectral measurements of the five star-forming regions in the different molecular lines. For observed objects obtained maps in the 13 molecular lines.

articleTitle: Texture region detection by trained neural network
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this paper we consider an important practical aspect of texture region detection in remote sensing images. One specific feature of our study is that we assume a processed image noisy with a priori known type and parameters of the noise. Another specific feature is that we try to detect textural regions for a wide variety of textures without having a priori knowledge of their properties. The considered task is solved by means of trained neural networks. In the paper, we analyze the aspects of choosing input local parameters used in detection (recognition) and carrying out training. The verification results provide valuable conclusions for these aspects.

articleTitle: Effect of solar flares on Schumann resonance frequencies
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Reaction is analyzed of Schumann resonance (SR) frequencies on the recent solar X-ray flares. Until now, no convincing evidence was presented for the influence of solar X-rays on the SR peak frequencies owing to its masking both by the regular diurnal variations and random fluctuations. We worked out a special technique that implies weighted average frequency (WAF) and thus reveals the simultaneous sharp variation present in all resonance modes. Statistical processing of experimental WAF allowed us to infer the relationship between the SR records and the intensity of solar X-rays: an increase of the weighted frequency is proportional to the logarithm of the X-ray intensity in the 1.7 power. The observed alterations of WAF were then assigned to equivalent alterations of the “magnetic” characteristic height of the “knee” profile of ionosphere conductivity. Finally, the extremely low frequency data were compared with the published results on the very low frequency transmissions.

articleTitle: Microwave spectrometer for Rydberg state atoms: Last improvements
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The results of essential improvement of the microwave spectrometer for investigation of spectra of Rydberg state atoms are presented. The spectrometer was equipped by a new time domain (waveform) acquisition system, which allowed us to apply time selection of useful signal. Such solution significantly improved signal-to-noise ratio of recorded spectra. The result of test measurement of a microwave transition between Rydberg states of magnesium atom is presented.

articleTitle: The absence of fixed cut-off frequencies in a circular layered waveguide with lossy liquid
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The wave propagation in a circular metal waveguide with a central cylindrical dielectric rod and coaxial layer of absorbing liquid have been studied at the frequency range 5-30 GHz. Owing to the absorbing liquid the operating frequencies range can be extended up to centimeter wavelength range. This fact takes place because of the two-layered waveguide with absorbing liquid does not have fixed cutoff frequencies for waveguide modes. It has been found abnormally low attenuation coefficients of electromagnetic waves HE11 in the centimeter wavelength range at certain frequencies and values of thickness of the absorbing liquid. The sensitivity of the method of complex permittivity determination of absorbing liquid using a thin liquid layer increases in comparison with a thick layer.

articleTitle: Forward Looking ground penetrating radar with synthetic antenna aperture for buried explosive hazards detection
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In the paper there are represented some results showing ability to detect of buried mines with use of Forward Looking GPR prototype developed on the basis of Stepped Frequency Continuous Wave probing signal and aperture synthesis technique realized by moving subarray consisting of one transmitter and one receiver to different locations forming the antenna array aperture.

articleTitle: Peculiarities of signal and noise characteristics of FMCW ayutodyne radar
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Calculations of phase, frequency and amplitude characteristics are performed as well as the output signal, which is registered in the power supply circuit of the autodyne oscillator with linear FM of radiation are carried out. Calculations are performed at different values of feedback parameter. At that, dependences of appropriate noise levels as functions of distance to reflector are given. The phenomenon of periodic non-stationarity of output signal noise levels is discovered under conditions of strong feedback. Calculations are performed in conformity with the autodyne oscillator on 8-mm Gunn diode.

articleTitle: Synthesis of optimal multiantenna radiometric 3D mapping complexes
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The spatially distributed object detection algorithms in the viewing zone and subsequent optimal formation of its 3D map are synthesized and investigated. The block diagram of radiometric complex is developed. The potential characteristics of the synthesized complex are investigated.

articleTitle: Tunable bandpass filter based on single-crystal platelet of BaFe12O19 in multidomain area
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Prototype of bandpass filter based on single-crystal platelet of hexaferrite in multidomain area with stripe domain structure in the initial state was proposed for the first time. Designed and experimentally studied filter has 3dB-bandwidth of 80 MHz within frequencies about 47 GHz in absence of external biasing magnetic field. The filter has insertion loss of 52 dB which can be significantly decreased with optimization of conditions for excitation and receiving of magnetostatic oscillations.

articleTitle: Dispersion relations for bulk and surface polaritons in a magnetic-semiconductor superlattice
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Dispersion relations for both bulk and surface polaritons in a subwavelength magnetic-semiconductor structure which is placed in an external static magnetic field, applied parallel to the boundaries of the layers are studied. It has been shown that the conditions of simultaneous existence of bulk and surface polaritons in the same spectral range can be reached in the system under consideration, providing a conscious choice of the constitutive parameters and material fractions for both magnetic and semiconductor subsystems.

articleTitle: Research of the underlying surface by radiation of global navigation satellite system
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The detection possibility of the reflection areas on the underlying surface and estimation of their parameters by using radiation of global navigation satellite systems are shown. The behavior of the signal levels for different satellites in urban areas is analyzed. The influence of the reflection area's characteristics on spectrum of the received radiations is considered. The method of determining the location of reflection areas is proposed.

articleTitle: Absorption of microwave radiation in a thin conducting fibers and protective screens creation
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Very strong absorption of microwave radiation is taking place in a conductive thin fiber which diameter is much smaller than the wavelength. This effect can be used to create protective screens.

articleTitle: Operation modes of the relativistic magnetron at millimeter wavelengths
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The operation of millimeter-wave relativistic magnetrons is considered for devices of the traditional and the inverted design. The high-voltage, pulsed devices employ explosive emission of electrons in electric fields about (1÷5)·10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> V/m near the emitting surface. The electric parameters like these allow magnetron generation with either polarity of the DC driving pulse, both in the traditional and inverted configuration, thus enabling four combinations of geometry and voltage polarity. The operation modes where the source of electrons is near the slow-wave structure have been studied for the first time.

articleTitle: Experimental studies of the 8-mm wave Gunn diode autodynes
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Data of the experimental studies of an energy potential and dynamic range of the normal and frequency stabilized by the external high-Q resonator autodynes based on planar 8-mm Gunn diodes are provided.

articleTitle: A method of loss determination in 1D gratings in the THz range
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this paper we present an experimental method of determining losses caused by 1D gratings based on applying those gratings as output couplers of THz lazers. Firstly we experimentally determined the optimal coupling coefficient for two types of gratings: wire gratings and strip gratings on dielectric substrates. Therefore we determined the value of total losses in laser cavity for each researched grating. Comparing these results it is possible to determine the losses caused by specific grating.

articleTitle: Use of information about the distribution of intensity for image restoration while observing through turbid media
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: An approach to the restoration of the image is distorted by turbid media is based on the use of a priori information about the form of distributions in the presence and lack of distortion is proposed. Examples of the use of the proposed approach for the restoration of the image when viewed through a turbid medium as contaminated water are shown.

articleTitle: Image reconstruction in complex media by the fourth moment wavelet
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The discrete wavelet transform (DWT) is generally used in digital image processing to compress or filter images, its operation is based on a quadrature mirror filter that can analyze images in different frequency components. The DWT decomposes images into different sub-matrices representing the original image but in different frequencies analysis. The sub-images obtained is the representation of a low-pass filter and high-pass filter (LL), low-pass filter and high-pass filter (LH), high-pass filter and low-pass filter (HL), finally high-pass filter and high-pass filter (HH). In these sub-images the average noise is zero, but when an image is sent in a wireless channel changes the nature of the image by performing a shift of the mean value. The noise added to images can be eliminated by designing filters with high complexity and high costs, sometimes is diminished the rate of sending and receiving data sent due to the above conditions. Digital images tend to visually impaired decreasing its quality and sometimes tends to lose relevant information about this. By applying the wavelet fourth moment as a mechanism for reconstruction of digital images in noisy environments, together with a reducing estimator of the mean square error, variance and standard deviation, as detector noise in the coefficients of the sub-matrix LH of wavelet decomposition results in simulations showing up to 31 dB for the PSNR.

articleTitle: Gyrotron FU II for a radiation source of THz ESR spectroscopy with a high field pulse magnet
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: For ESR spectroscopy covering sub THz to THz region, we have developed a frequency-step tunable Gyrotron FU II as a radiation source. A pulse magnet is used for high field ESR spectroscopy. The pulse width is around 50 ms. In order to cover this pulse width, the gyrotron can operate during more than 100 ms in pulse length.

articleTitle: Plasmon resonances in two-layered circular graphene shells
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: We address surface and volume resonance in two concentric cylindrical graphene shells driven by the H-polarized plane wave of the THz range. Modeling implies analytical solution of the wave scattering in presence of impedance boundary conditions at thin graphene shells. Cases are considered of graphene positioned in the free space and at the inner and outer sides of a dielectric tube. Spectra of normalized scatter and absorption cross-sections are presented together with the spatial distributions of the field in the vicinity of object. These reveal hybrid resonance of surface plasmons and the eigen-waves in separating dielectric tube.

articleTitle: Investigation of radiation characteristics of fresnal antenna
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Diffraction problems on planar ring structure are considered. The field structure on reflector antenna is analyzed. Radiation properties of the antenna are measurements.

articleTitle: Optical Coherence Tomography of semitransparent media: Analysis of the method
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) is a modern technique suited for high-resolution, real-time, in-vivo and in-situ imaging of biological tissue. OCT can provide images with a micron-level resolution, higher than in other known medical imaging methods, such as ultrasound, magnetic resonance imaging and computed tomography. Since the early 1990s, OCT has been widely used in medical applications as a non-invasive, safe and inexpensive imaging technique. Over time, basic principles of OCT, various approaches, measurement setups and devices have been described in many publications and reports. However, some theoretical aspects of OCT are not yet covered in-depth, in particular, the questions related to statistical analysis and statistical modelling of this imaging technique. This paper revisits the problem of spectral domain OCT using a mathematical approach stemming from radar signal processing, which combines Fourier-based analysis and statistical (correlation) analysis. In this context, the broadband signal from the low-coherence light source is represented in the time and spectral domains, and the object signal is modeled as the complex scattering coefficient of the test semitransparent media. We showed how the proposed approach can be used for statistical simulation of OCT imaging. The results presented in this work are achieved for the first time.

articleTitle: Two-stream superheterodyne free electron lasers as formers of ultrashort electromagnetic clusters
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: We develop a cubic nonlinear self-consistent theory of multiharmonic two-stream superheterodyne free electron lasers (TSFEL) of a klystron type, designed to form powerful ultrashort clusters of an electromagnetic field. We have considered plural three-wave parametric resonant interactions of wave harmonics. We used the TSFEL regime in which the first harmonic of a space-charge wave (SCW) is much smaller than the critical frequency of two-stream instability for forming of the powerful ultrashort clusters of electromagnetic waves. Amplitude, phase and spectral analyses of the processes occurring in such devices have been carried out. We found out the conditions needed for the forming of the ultrashort electromagnetic field clusters. We demonstrate the possibility of the ultrashort electromagnetic cluster formation in the multiharmonic TSFEL-type systems.

articleTitle: Definition permittivity of weakly concentrated solutions in the microwave range
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this paper a modification of the well-known method of resonance dielectrometry is proposed with the aim to define a real part of the permittivity of weakly concentrated solutions in the microwave frequency band. By using the results of numerical simulations, the optimized electrodynamical module has been fabricated and tested. The experimental verification of the proposed method points out the high sensitivity and accuracy of measurements.

articleTitle: Non-Hermitian Hamiltonian approach for electromagnetic wave propagation and dissipation in dielectric media
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Using the formal analogy between a certain class of Maxwell equations and the Schrdinger equation, we derive the effective Hamiltonian operator that governs the propagation of electromagnetic (EM) wave modes inside nonconducting linear media, which include a large range of nanophotonic and plasmonic waveguides. It turns out that this Hamiltonian is essentially non-Hermitian, and thus requires a special treatment. We formulate the density operator approach for dynamical systems with non-Hermitian Hamiltonians, and derive a master equation that describes the statistical ensembles of EM wave modes. The method provides a theoretical instrument which can be used when designing the next generation of quantum EM devices for sensitive and non-invasive measurements.

articleTitle: InBN and GaBN graded gap Gunn diodes at different BN distribution
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The usage of graded-gap semiconductors can increase the efficiency and output power of Gunn generators. The energy gap between the valleys in InBN and GaBN compounds, unlike other ternary semiconductor nitrides, can be reduced to zero. This gives the opportunity to find the optimal distribution of the BN component in graded gap compounds for Gunn diodes. In this paper we present the results of numerical experiments on the oscillation generation in the range from 300 to 700 GHz using the n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>-n-n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> Gunn diodes based on InBN and GaBN graded gap semiconductor compounds at different BN distribution. We have estimated the cutoff frequency of mentioned diodes. For the efficiency we have found out that at optimal BN distribution graded-gap semiconductor InBN and GaBN Gunn diodes exceed GaN and InN diodes in more than two times. We also have found out that power consumption of graded-gap InBN and GaBN diodes is 11÷19% less the power consumption of InN and GaN diodes.

articleTitle: Chiral properties of bulk metamaterial with metallized polylactide helical elements
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The technology of quickly formation of bulk metamaterials with a complicated structure was designed. The bulk chiral metamaterial with a cell on the basis of helical element with a sufficiently large effective chirality parameter in the microwave frequency range has been constructed. It has been demonstrated experimentally that even 2 micrometer layer of the Al-metallization of elements leads to sufficient chiral properties of the metamaterial in the vicinity of frequency 22 GHz.

articleTitle: Modification of cellular effects of exposure to gamma-radiation by microwaves and magnetic field
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Cellular effects of exposure to gamma-radiation in combination with magnetic field and microwave radiation have been investigated. The degree of chromatin condensation and permeability of cytoplasmic membrane in exfoliated human buccal epithelium cells have been evaluated. The exposure of cells to gamma-radiation induced chromatin condensation and cell membrane damage. Strong correlation between changes in heterochromatinization and cells' membrane permeability has been proved. Protective and recovery effects of low-dose microwave radiation exposure have been shown on gamma radiation-induced chromatin condensation and cells membrane damage. Exposure to magnetic field revealed such an effect only in the case of chromatin condensation.

articleTitle: Stimulating effect of the terahertz band electromagnetic radiation
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Mobility of human buccal epithelium cell nuclei was investigated using the method of intracellular micro-electrophoresis before and after the influence of the terahertz gas laser. As the result of the experiments it was noted a substantial variation of electrophoretic activity of the nuclei that witnessed for a stimulating effect of the terahertz band electromagnetic radiation.

articleTitle: Analysis of the H-polarized electromagnetic wave diffraction by an infinite periodical strip grating without one strip
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Analysis of the electrodynamical properties of the infinite periodical grating without one strip is performed in this paper. The H-polarization case is considered. The mathematical model is based on the singular integral equations method. Scattered field is presented as sum of three summands: field of the infinite periodical grating, field of a single strip of the infinite periodical grating and correction field. The directional patterns and field distribution are represented.

articleTitle: Microwave phase-locking of two weakly-coupled spin-torque nano-oscillators with random eigen parameters
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Microwave dynamics of the system of two weakly-coupled spin-torque nano-oscillators (STNOs) was analyzed. It was shown that synchronization criterion of such STNO system is a small variation of the modulus of the complex order parameter over time. Using this criterion a microwave synchronization of STNOs with random eigen frequencies (Gaussian distribution) and initial phases (rectangular distribution) has been studied numerically.

articleTitle: Simulation of the electron magnetic resonance peak shape for Fe3O4 nanopowder
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Results of simulation of the electron spin resonance absorption peak shape for the magnetic nanopowder are presented. The influence of the magnetic particle diameter on the shape and on the width of the resonance peak is shown. Simulation results show a good agreement with the experimental data of the electron spin resonance absorption in the Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> nanopoweder.

articleTitle: Submillimetric localization of microwave diagnostics and modification of objects of various nature
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The analysis of the conditions and possibilities of localized electromagnetic fields formation was conducted via coaxial microprobe structures and their use for the diagnosis of electrophysical parameters and local heat influence.

articleTitle: Bispectral-based signal processing technique for digital communication system
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Paper is dedicated to novel bispectrum-based signal processing technique using triple-channel heterodyning procedure performed for triplet-signals in digital communication systems. Test statistics exploited for detection and discrimination of triplet-signals are evaluated in the form of the bimagnitude peak values according to the maximum likelihood rule. Novel strategy developed for fast bispectrum-based signal processing is suggested. Experimental study of noise immunity in bispectrum-based digital communication system is carried out for suggested triple-channel heterodyning technique. Bit error rate (BER) values are computed under influence of additive Gaussian noise in radio communication link for wide range of variations of input signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).

articleTitle: Waveguide-slot coupling element partially filled with dielectric
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Scattering parameters of a slotted diaphragm in a rectangular waveguide are studied. The transverse slot in the diaphragm is partially filled with dielectric. The mathematical model includes accounting several spatial harmonics for description the electrical field in the slot. Resonance wavelength dependence on geometrical structure and electrical parameters of the insert in the slot is revealed. Comparison of experimental and calculated data is given.

articleTitle: Spectral properties of 3-D spherical microwave resonator by using FDTD simulation
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Cavity microwave resonators are the most known physical modeling apps of microwave billiard system depending of its geometry and dielectric filling. In this paper we apply finite difference time domain (FDTD) method to study properties of frequency spectrum of the microwave spherical 3-D resonator. We obtained probability distribution of inter-frequency intervals and spectral rigidity using frequency resonator spectrum. These dependences practically coincide with Poisson distribution that corresponds to integrable systems.

articleTitle: Acoustic birefringence at electromagnetic excitation of sound in iron borate crystals
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In the antiferromagnetic single crystal of iron borate the effect of electromagnetic generation of the sound of transverse polarization is studied. In an external magnetic field the acoustic birefringence is detected. Data on the magnitude of magnetoelastic gap are obtained.

articleTitle: The torsional fundamental band and submillimeter wave spectrum of acetone
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: A new study of the acetone (CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>CO spectrum is reported. The measurements covering the frequency range from 34 GHz to 940 GHz have been carried out using spectrometers in IRA NASU (Ukraine) and PhLAM Lille (France). The far infrared spectrum of acetone has been recorded on the AILES beamline of the synchrotron SOLEIL using a Fourier transform infrared spectrometer coupled to a long path cell. The transitions belonging to the three lowest torsional states as well as to the observed fundamental band associated with the methyl-top torsion mode (ν<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</inf>=1) have been analyzed using recently developed model for the molecules with two equivalent methyl rotors and C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2v</inf> symmetry at equilibrium (PAM_C2v_2tops program). The dataset consisting of more than 26100 microwave and 1100 FIR line frequencies and including transitions with J up to 89 was fit using a model consisting of 119 parameters and weighted root-mean-square deviation of 0.89 has been achieved.

articleTitle: Pulse surface wave in closed circular waveguide with dielectric rod pulse surface wave
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: During a pulse signal propagation in a dielectric waveguide pulse surface wave can be excited. This wave represents a “precursor” of wave structure. Above mentioned wave have some parts inside the dielectric rod and near the rod surface. The field distribution for this wave inside the dielectric rod is a rhombus-shape and consists of cones similar to Cherenkov wavefront. A part of this wave propagates in free space near the dielectric surface with the speed of light in free space. This wave propagates along the waveguide with the speed of light in free space as a whole wave structure. Such a guided wave structure differs from conventional waveguide modes since it does not have the same transverse field distribution in any cross-section. First this effect was investigated as a wave structure created by a localized source inside the open dielectric waveguide. The aim of this paper is to consider excitation of such a wave in closed circular waveguide with a dielectric rod and explore the possibility to create some resonance devices using this wave type. For the calculations BOR-FDTD method was used with PML boundary conditions.

articleTitle: Influence of absorbent layer on nonlinear microwave properties of HTS-based coplanar waveguide
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The paper presents the results of continuing experimental studies of a coplanar waveguide on the basis of YBCO thin film (75 nm) depending on the input power and DC level. It is shown that use of a highly absorbent material on the back side of the substrate changes HTS transition characteristics in a strongly dissipative state. Apparently it is caused by a changing in the heat transfer between the structure and the helium gas filling the structure chamber. This fact leads to a decreasing the value of DC corresponding to a structure transition to a highly dissipative state.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of methods for estimation of parameters of the ionosphere by tweek atmospherics
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Comparative analysis of two different methods for estimation of parameters of the lower ionosphere by tweek - atmospherics was performed. These are so-called the phase and the sonogram methods. The analysis is based on numerical simulations of tweek atmospherics waveforms. The dependency of estimations accuracy of distance to a tweek source and effective ionosphere height were tested against a stochastic noise level. The stochastic error decreases with increasing SNR. The maximum value of the systematic error for SNR = 5dB is of 4% for distance and 1% for height estimations.

articleTitle: Effect of DC magnetic field on reflectivity of layered superconductors
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The possibility to control waves reflectivity by means of external DC magnetic field has special interest, since the magnetic field represent a flexible tool to manipulate the electromagnetic properties of layered superconductors. In the present work we study the effect of external DC magnetic field on the reflection of transverse-magnetic (TM) waves of terahertz range from a semi-infinite sample of layered superconductor. We obtain the analytical expression for reflectivity and show that the presence of DC magnetic field can either increase or decrease the reflectance depending on the problem parameters. Special attention is focused on the minimization of reflectance as a function of incident angle, static magnetic field and wave frequency. The obtained results can be used in terahertz detectors and filters designing.

articleTitle: Experimental study of atmosphere turbulence by using bicoherence-based signal processing technique
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Novel bispectrum-based signal processing technique is proposed for analysis of turbulence contained in the atmosphere. Novel classification features evaluated in the form of bicoherence estimates of the weather radar signals backscattered by volume-distributed atmospheric formations are suggested for solving the discrimination problem of the safe laminar meteorological formations and zones of turbulence dangerous for the aircraft flights. Results of experimental measurements performed by non-coherent double-frequency weather radar operating in millimeter and centimeter wavelength ranges are represented and discussed.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic waves in the searchlight beam of antenna arrays large electrical size
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Studied theoretically the amplitude and phase characteristics of electromagnetic fields in the near and intermediate zones of observation antenna arrays large electrical size with square and round aperture. The existence of a searchlight beam in such arrays at any distance between radiators is proved. Shown that if the distances between radiators larger wavelength, searchlight beam is formed at some distance from the antenna.

articleTitle: Impact of major carrier concentration in silicon on transparence of photonic crystal
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: This paper dedicated to numerical and experimental investigations of the role of majority carrier concentration in the silicon in the transmission coefficients of photonic crystals created from quartz and silicon layers in microwave frequency range. The silicon of two types of conductivity has been viewed. The impact of majority carrier concentration on the transparence in allowed bands of photonic crystals is shown.

articleTitle: The matrix radiometric system for the imaging of ground objects in the millimeter band
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Justified practical implementation matrix radiometric systems (multibeam antennas and multichannel radiometric receivers), designed to create images of ground objects on board aircraft for various purposes. Formation of two-dimensional images in a short time exposure as possible due to the application of the matrix radiometric information sensors, and with the use of multi-channel radiometric sensors based multiplexing with separation in the form of signals using the Walsh function.

articleTitle: SAR tomography of forested areas: An APES-based virtual beamforming approach
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The main purpose of synthetic aperture radar tomography (T-SAR) is to retrieve the vertical distribution of the backscattered power within a range-azimuth resolution cell, allowing three dimensional (3-D) imaging of volumetric targets. The achievable resolution of conventional spectral estimators, used to tackle with the T-SAR vertical distribution estimation problem, highly depends on the span of the tomographic aperture and on the number of acquisitions, reason why, adaptive spectral estimators were introduced in order to ease such limitations. This paper proposes a novel amplitude and phase estimation (APES) -based virtual beamforming approach aimed at resolution enhanced SAR tomography of forested areas, which functions properly using only a few passes and arbitrary constellation geometries, and with imaging capabilities comparable to those gotten from super-resolution compressed sensing spectral estimators with the sum of Kronecker products decomposition technique as a pre-processing step.

articleTitle: Methodical features of dark objects detection by using gravitational refraction
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: We investigate the possibility of discovering the dark space objects by bending action of their gravitational field on the trajectory of a passing light. Considering the large distances between reference radiation sources and their small angular dimensions, we propose a very simple algorithm for solving the inverse problem of tomographic detection of dark objects.

articleTitle: Method of correlation-spectrum analysis for target identification
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The method of detection and identification of a low Doppler target under conditions of intensive disturbances having fluctuating character is investigated in this article. The proposed algorithm for calculating the estimations of the target spatial position and the Doppler frequency translation of a signal reflected from the target is an optimum from the standpoint of the maximum of likelihood. The algorithm was based on the principle of the combined processing of signals from spaced sensors in order to obtain the optimum estimations of signal parameters. The analysis is carried out both in the spectral and in the time domains which makes it possible to extract a maximum amount of information about the object under investigation with disturbances of different character and level. The results of the algorithm modelling are presented; the characteristic features of its performance in actual practice are discussed.

articleTitle: Structural synthesis of radiometric systems for topography
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The problem of structural synthesis of ultra-wideband radiometric systems is solved for mapping the underlying surface. For synthesized signal processing algorithm proving the simulation in MATLAB has been performed. The potential accuracy of the formation of the relief is found.

articleTitle: Investigation of microwave power generation of pulse double-drift Si IMPATT diodes operating in short part of millimeter wave lengths
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: This article presents the results of studies experimental samples of silicon drift impact ionization avalanche transit-time (IMPATT) diodes and generators on its basis. On silicic double-drift region IMPATT diode with round quartz pillar it was obtained microwave generation with frequency of 227 GHz and launch power 16,6 mW with the pulse duration of 80 ns. Also, there are parameters of IMPATT oscillator, structural decisions used for the concordance of impedance of IMPATT diode with microwave cell and charts of measuring tract.

Author Keywords: short part of millimeter wave lengths

articleTitle: Optimization of shielding effectiveness of coaxial double braided screens in contact
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this paper, the optimization of the shielding effectiveness of double braided coaxial screens in contact is obtained using semi-empirical single braid optimization formulas. Also the effect of the mutual inductance term between the double braided screens in contact is investigated. A sample optimization has been obtained practically, on one of the standard double braided RF coaxial cable namely, RG-142.

articleTitle: A two-stage procedure of radar target detection
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: A two-stage procedure is suggested for detection of radar targets against a noise background using a sequence of radar echoes from a spatial cell under test. According to the procedure a standard decision making procedure is first applied to each sample. Then the final “target-present” decision is taken if the detection threshold is exceeded in no less than a preset quantity of the total number of the radar samples under analysis. Expressions for the detection probability and false alarm rate are presented. Performance characteristics of the suggested algorithm are analyzed for the case of detection of stationary Gaussian signals against a normal noise background. It is shown that under certain conditions the developed technique provides an improvement in the signal-to-noise ratio as compared with the coherent and incoherent averaging techniques.

articleTitle: Accurate simulation of 2D periodic structures excitation by an obliquely incident plane wave
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: New simulation technique of a 2D periodic structure excitation by an electromagnetic wave incident an arbitrary angle is suggested. The approach is based on the statement that all pulsed fields arising in the reflection and transmission areas of a periodic structure are unambiguously determined by their own longitudinal components. We use ordinary Yee grid that allows us to implement computer simulation of an incident wave with FDTD algorithm.

articleTitle: On the characteristic equation for the dielectric-loaded circular waveguide
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The representations for asymmetrical modes and characteristic equation for the dielectric-loaded circular waveguide are proposed. They have no singularities at the critical points. The proposed representations are convenient for calculation of a plane junction of a dielectric-loaded circular waveguide with another waveguide.

articleTitle: Audiometer controlled by brain waves
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)

authors.preferredName: M. en C. Ismael Gabriel Cosme Cisneros

abstract: Nowadays, that people have hearing diseases are more common but how to diagnose remain the same as fifty years ago. The audiometry has been the most common study and this is to determine the hearing threshold of the patient. Because we inducing sounds at different frequencies and power through earphones and the patient indicates the moment when he perceives sound, we can conclude that audiometry is a subjective test. In this paper developed a more reliable system for determining hearing threshold and operation is with brain waves analysis generated in the moment when the brain captures the different sounds frequencies.

articleTitle: An algorithm for recognition of hydrometeors by polarimetric radar data based on the information theory
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: For recognition of meteorological objects a two-stage algorithm based on the information theory and on the statistical decision theory for a vector space of polarimetric signatures is developed. General description and the results of the algorithm testing performed on modeled radar signals backscattered by specific classes of hydrometeors as well as on the data received in full-scale experiments are given in the paper.

articleTitle: Analysis of measurement error of porous dielectric permittivity
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Resonance structures of the waveguide-dielectric type are the matter for the scientific investigations contributing to the development of the resonators of new modifications with the improved parameters. In the paper two methods for the measurement of the small permittivity of materials using the resonators on the basis of a cylindrical evanescent waveguide have been discussed.

articleTitle: Investigation of starting position of the magnetron with cold cathode
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Experimentally is investigational influence of operating mode and steepness of pulse wavefront of anodic voltage on the magnitude of auxiliary thermionic cathode current of necessary for the start of magnetron with a secondary-emission cathode. It is shown that the size of this current increases with the increase of anodic voltage and steepness of pulse front.

articleTitle: Application of double-diode autodynes in control systems for technological processes
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Options and application opportunities of double-diode autodynes in microwave sensors are considered to radio-wave control dimensions of products, vibration and displacement parameters, velocity and movement direction of reflecting objects.

articleTitle: Strip gratings on dielectric substrates electrodynamic parameters measurement in the THz range
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: This paper presents the analysis of application of strip gratings on dielectric substrates as output couplers for submillimeter lasers. The coupler transmittance characteristics was calculated by FDTD method and compared with experimental results. The influence of the dielectric substrate on the coupler transmittance was investigated.

articleTitle: Signatures of acousto-electromagnetic portraits of aerodynamic and terrestrial mechanical objects
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The possibility of creating a dictionary of signs for the radar recognition of the aerodynamic and terrestrial mechanical objects through the use of data about as dimensions of the objects, and the acoustic noise is analyzed. RCS of aerodynamic objects at resonant and short wavelengths as well as their speeds of revolution are estimated.

articleTitle: Specific features of electrodynamic characteristics for double-row periodic systems based on diffraction bar gratings
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Electrodynamic characteristics of double-row periodic systems which are formed by metal bar gratings of rectangular cross-section under their excitation by dielectric waveguide disposed along their longitudinal axis are described. The possibility of effective adjustment of the power level of emitted harmonics and of oscillation selection by changing the longitudinal and angular coordinates of a double-row periodic structure is presented.

articleTitle: Diffraction radiation oscillator with the asymmetric open resonant system
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The results of the experimental investigations and 2-D modeling of the asymmetric open resonant system properties for the diffraction radiation oscillator, in which the periodic structure is displaced on the periphery of the field spot of the operating TEM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">00q</sub>-mode, are presented. It was established, that the asymmetric placement of the periodic structure, in the double grating form, on the plane mirror of the hemispherical open resonator allows to reduce ohmic and diffraction loss of the operating TEM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">00q</sub>-mode and significantly extend the range of the single-mode tuning. The investigations are carried out in 8-mm waveband.

articleTitle: Synthesis & characterization of tetrahedrite compounds for thermoelectric applications
publicationTitle: 2016 9th International Kharkiv Symposium on Physics and Engineering of Microwaves, Millimeter and Submillimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Thermoelectric materials have attracted much attention due to their potential applications in conversion of heat into electrical power or vice versa to cool the heat-generating elements using electrical power. Tetrahedrite is copper antimony sulfosalt mineral with the formula of Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>Sb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</inf>, where Cu could be partially replaced by another 3d (Mn, Ag, Al, Cr, Zn, Fe) or other (4d,5d) metal.
